```{r}
#| label: setup
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "sf", "rnaturalearth", "rnaturalearthdata",
#                    "ggrepel", "scales", "knitr"))
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, ggplot2, readr, lubridate, ...
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(ggrepel)
library(scales)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))

partial_year <- 2026   # year with incomplete data
SIAP_col <- "#1b6ca8"

```

# 1. Import and cleaning

```{r}
#| label: import
# The file is Windows-1252 encoded (not UTF-8)
raw <- read_csv(
  "Data/Course_List.csv",
  locale = locale(encoding = "windows-1252"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

df <- raw |>
  select(where(~ !all(is.na(.x)))) |>                 # drop empty trailing columns
  rename(NbPart = `N part`, NWomen = `N Female`) |>   # rename columns
  mutate(
    across(c(NbPart, NWomen), as.numeric),
    PctWomen = 100 * NWomen / NbPart                  # % of women
  )
```

## 1.1 Clean `Form`

Rules: `F`, `B` → **F2F**; `EL`, `W` → **EL**. Missing values are inferred from
`Category type` (E-learn / Webinar → EL, anything else → F2F).

```{r}
#| label: clean-form
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    Form_raw      = Form,
    Form_inferred = is.na(Form_raw),
    cat_type      = str_to_lower(str_squish(`Category type`)),
    Form          = str_to_upper(str_squish(Form)),
    Form = case_when(
      Form %in% c("F", "B")                                   ~ "F2F",
      Form %in% c("EL", "W")                                  ~ "EL",
      is.na(Form) & str_detect(cat_type, "e-learn|webinar")   ~ "EL",
      is.na(Form) & !is.na(cat_type)                          ~ "F2F",
      TRUE                                                    ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

df |> count(Form_raw, Form) |> knitr::kable(caption = "Form: raw vs cleaned")
```

Rows where `Form` was inferred:

```{r}
#| label: inferred-rows
df |>
  filter(Form_inferred) |>
  select(Year, Topics, `Category type`, Location, Form) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

Sanity checks: face-to-face courses without a country, and inconsistent counts.

```{r}
#| label: checks
df |>
  filter(Form == "F2F", is.na(Country)) |>
  count(Location, name = "n_F2F_without_country") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "F2F courses whose Location is not in the lookup (or is '-')")

df |>
  filter(NWomen > NbPart) |>
  select(Year, Topics, NbPart, NWomen) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Rows where NWomen > NbPart")
```

```{r}
#| label: f2f
f2f <- df |> filter(Form == "F2F", !is.na(Country))
last_start <- max(mdy(df$`Start date`), na.rm = TRUE)
```

# 2. Overview by year

```{r}
#| label: yearly-table
yearly <- df |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(
    n_courses = n(),
    NbPart    = sum(NbPart, na.rm = TRUE),
    NWomen    = sum(NWomen, na.rm = TRUE),
    # % women only on rows where both counts exist
    PctWomen  = 100 * sum(NWomen[!is.na(NbPart) & !is.na(NWomen)]) /
                      sum(NbPart[!is.na(NbPart) & !is.na(NWomen)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(partial = Year >= partial_year)

yearly |>
  select(Year, n_courses, NbPart, NWomen, PctWomen) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

*Missing `NbPart` / `NWomen` values are ignored in the sums.
`r partial_year` is a **partial year** (data up to `r format(last_start, "%d %B %Y")`).*

# 3. Evolution of the number of participants

## 3.1 Total

```{r}
#| label: plot-total
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(yearly, aes(Year, NbPart)) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, Year < partial_year), linewidth = 1,
            colour = SIAP_col) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, Year >= partial_year - 1), linewidth = 1,
            colour = SIAP_col, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = partial), size = 3.5, colour = SIAP_col, stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(NbPart)), vjust = -1.2, size = 3.3) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 18),
                     labels = c("Full year", "Partial year"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(yearly$Year)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Number of participants per year",
       x = NULL, y = "NbPart",
       caption = paste0(partial_year, " is a partial year (courses up to ",
                        format(last_start, "%d %b %Y"), ")."))
```


```{r}
#| label: plot-total-smooth
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5

# =====================================================================
#  >>>  SMOOTHING PARAMETER (edit me)  <<<
#  loess span: share of points used for each local fit.
#    small (0.5)  -> curve follows the points closely (wiggly)
#    large (1.0+) -> very smooth, close to a straight trend
#  With about 11 yearly points, stay roughly between 0.5 and 1.2.
smooth_span <- 0.6
# =====================================================================

# Fit on complete years only; 2026 is partial, so it is predicted, not fitted
full <- filter(yearly, Year < partial_year)

# degree = 1 and surface = "direct" make extrapolation to 2026 possible and stable
fit <- loess(NbPart ~ Year, data = full, span = smooth_span, degree = 1,
             control = loess.control(surface = "direct"))

curve <- tibble(Year = seq(min(full$Year), partial_year, length.out = 200)) |>
  mutate(fit = predict(fit, newdata = pick(Year)))

pred_2026 <- slice_tail(curve, n = 1)   # predicted full-year value for 2026



ggplot() +
  # solid smooth curve up to 2025, dashed from 2025 to the 2026 prediction
  geom_line(data = filter(curve, Year <= partial_year - 1),
            aes(Year, fit), colour = SIAP_col, linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_line(data = filter(curve, Year >= partial_year - 1),
            aes(Year, fit), colour = SIAP_col, linewidth = 1.2, linetype = "dashed") +
  # observed points, as before (hollow = partial year)
  geom_point(data = yearly, aes(Year, NbPart, shape = partial),
             size = 3, colour = SIAP_col, stroke = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = yearly, aes(Year, NbPart, label = comma(NbPart)),
            vjust = -1.2, size = 3.3, colour = SIAP_col) +
  # predicted 2026 (full-year trend value)
  geom_point(data = pred_2026, aes(Year, fit), shape = 3, size = 4,
             colour = SIAP_col) +
  # geom_text(data = pred_2026,
  #           aes(Year, fit, label = paste0("Predicted ", partial_year, ": ",
  #                                         comma(round(fit)))),
  #           colour = "#c0392b", hjust = 1, vjust = 2, size = 3.3,
  #           fontface = "bold") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 18), 
                     labels = c("Full year", "Partial data (observed)"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(yearly$Year)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Number of participants per year",
       subtitle = paste0("Smoothed trend (", min(full$Year), "-",
                         max(full$Year), "). 2026 partial"),
       x = NULL, y = "Nb Participants",
       caption = paste0("Dashed curve (2025 to ", partial_year,
                        ") is extrapolated prediction.\n"))+
       theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```




## 3.2 Decomposition: EL vs F2F

```{r}
#| label: by-form-data
by_form <- df |>
  filter(!is.na(Form)) |>
  group_by(Year, Form) |>
  summarise(NbPart = sum(NbPart, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  complete(Year, Form, fill = list(NbPart = 0)) |>
  mutate(partial = Year >= partial_year)

by_form_total <- bind_rows(
  by_form,
  by_form |> group_by(Year, partial) |>
    summarise(NbPart = sum(NbPart), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(Form = "Total")
)

form_cols <- c(F2F = SIAP_col, EL = "#e08a1e", Total = "grey30")
```

**Lines** (with total):

```{r}
#| label: plot-form-lines
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(by_form_total, aes(Year, NbPart, colour = Form, group = Form)) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, Year < partial_year), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, Year >= partial_year - 1), linewidth = 1,
            linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = partial), size = 3, stroke = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = form_cols, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 1),
                     labels = c("Full year", "Partial year"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(by_form$Year)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Participants per year: e-learning (EL) vs face-to-face (F2F)",
       x = NULL, y = "NbPart",
       caption = paste0(partial_year, " is a partial year."))
```

**Stacked columns:**

```{r}
#| label: plot-form-stacked
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(by_form, aes(Year, NbPart, fill = Form, alpha = partial)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = form_cols[c("F2F", "EL")],
                    labels = c("F2F" = "Face-to-Face", "EL" = "E-Learning"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 0.5), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(by_form$Year)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Participants per year by format",
       x = NULL, y = "Nb Participants",
       caption = paste0("Data for ", partial_year, " (lighter bars) are partial.")) +
       theme(legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.01, 0.9))    

```

# 4. Countries

```{r}
#| label: n-countries
n_countries_all    <- n_distinct(f2f$Country)
n_countries_abroad <- n_distinct(f2f$Country[f2f$Country != "Japan"])
```

Face-to-face courses with a known location took place in
**`r n_countries_all` different countries/territories**
(`r n_countries_abroad` outside Japan). Guam and New Caledonia are counted as
separate territories.

```{r}
#| label: countries-year
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
countries_year <- f2f |>
  group_by(Year) |>
  summarise(n_countries = n_distinct(Country), n_courses = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(partial = Year >= partial_year)

ggplot(countries_year, aes(Year, n_countries, alpha = partial)) +
  geom_col(fill = SIAP_col, width = 0.75) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n_countries), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.3, alpha = 1) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 0.5), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(countries_year$Year)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Number of different countries hosting F2F courses",
       x = NULL, y = "Countries",
       caption = paste0(partial_year, " (lighter bar) is a partial year."))
```

```{r}
#| label: country-table
f2f |>
  group_by(Country) |>
  summarise(n_courses = n(), n_cities = n_distinct(City),
            NbPart = sum(NbPart, na.rm = TRUE),
            NWomen = sum(NWomen, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(n_courses)) |>
  knitr::kable(format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "F2F courses by country")
```

# 5. Maps of F2F courses

North-up world maps (Robinson projection, centred on 140°E so that the Pacific
is not cut), with arrows starting from **Chiba, Japan**. Only F2F courses with a
known location are shown; **no arrow is drawn for Chiba (or Tokyo)**, i.e. for
Japan. Arrows point to the city of the course; when only a country was recorded,
they point to its capital.

The arrows are curved flows that always bow northwards, with a bow proportional
to the distance. Routes to the west (Turkey, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan...) therefore
follow different paths instead of sitting on top of each other. Change
`curvature` in `make_curves()` to bend them more or less (0 = straight lines).

```{r}
#| label: map-data
chiba_lon <- 140.1233
chiba_lat <- 35.6073

# Robinson projection centred on 140E: north is up, Pacific in the middle
crs_map <- "+proj=robin +lon_0=140 +datum=WGS84 +units=m"

# Project lon/lat columns to map coordinates (px, py)
add_xy <- function(d) {
  xy <- d |>
    st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
    st_transform(crs_map) |>
    st_coordinates()
  d |> mutate(px = xy[, 1], py = xy[, 2])
}

# Chiba = origin of all arrows
origin <- add_xy(tibble(lon = chiba_lon, lat = chiba_lat))
x0 <- origin$px
y0 <- origin$py

# Destinations: one row per city (excluding Japan)
dest <- f2f |>
  filter(Country != "Japan") |>
  group_by(Country, iso3, City, lon, lat) |>
  summarise(n_courses = n(), n_part = sum(NbPart, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  add_xy()

# Destinations: one row per country (arrow goes to the city with most courses)
main_city <- dest |>
  group_by(Country) |>
  slice_max(n_courses, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(Country, City, px, py)

dest_country <- dest |>
  group_by(Country, iso3) |>
  summarise(n_courses = sum(n_courses), n_part = sum(n_part), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(main_city, by = "Country") |>
  mutate(label = paste0(Country, " (", n_courses, ")"))

# Basemap. No polygon clipping (st_intersection / st_make_valid) is used, which
# avoids s2 / GEOS topology errors on some Natural Earth polygons.
# The Americas and Greenland are dropped: they straddle the cut meridian of this
# projection (40W) and are far outside the map window anyway.
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") |>
  filter(!continent %in% c("Antarctica", "North America", "South America"))
iso_col <- intersect(c("iso_a3_eh", "iso_a3"), names(world))[1]
world$iso3 <- world[[iso_col]]

world_p <- world |>
  select(iso3, name) |>
  st_transform(crs_map)

# Map window: lon 10E to 165W, lat 30S to 68N (widen if a label is cut off)
ext <- add_xy(tibble(lon = c(10, -165, 140, 140), lat = c(0, 0, -30, 68)))
map_xlim <- range(ext$px[1:2])
map_ylim <- range(ext$py[3:4])

chiba_pt <- data.frame(x = x0, y = y0)

map_decor <- list(
  geom_point(data = chiba_pt, aes(x, y), shape = 21, size = 4,
             fill = "black", colour = "white", stroke = 1),
  geom_text(data = chiba_pt, aes(x, y, label = "Chiba"), nudge_y = -4e5,
            fontface = "bold", size = 3.5),
  coord_sf(crs = crs_map, xlim = map_xlim, ylim = map_ylim, expand = FALSE),
  theme_void(),
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),   # white ocean
        plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
        legend.position  = "right",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
)

# Curved flow from Chiba to each row of d (columns px, py).
# Quadratic Bezier; the arc always bows north, east- or west-bound.
make_curves <- function(d, curvature = 0.2, n = 60) {
  d <- d |> mutate(curve_id = row_number())
  t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
  map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(d)), \(i) {
    dx <- d$px[i] - x0
    dy <- d$py[i] - y0
    s  <- if (dx >= 0) 1 else -1
    cx <- x0 + dx / 2 - s * curvature * dy
    cy <- y0 + dy / 2 + s * curvature * dx
    tibble(curve_id = d$curve_id[i],
           x = (1 - t)^2 * x0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cx + t^2 * d$px[i],
           y = (1 - t)^2 * y0 + 2 * (1 - t) * t * cy + t^2 * d$py[i])
  }) |>
    left_join(d, by = "curve_id")
}

# World polygons joined with a country-level `value` column (needs `iso3`)
shade_world <- function(stat) {
  world_p |> left_join(select(stat, iso3, value), by = "iso3")
}

# Japan = origin: dark grey, left out of the colour scales
japan_layer <- geom_sf(data = filter(world_p, iso3 == "JPN"),
                       fill = "grey55", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2)

arrow_head <- arrow(length = unit(0.22, "cm"), type = "closed")
map_caption <- paste0("F2F courses ", min(df$Year), "-", max(df$Year),
                      " (", partial_year, " partial).")

# Country-level statistics (outside Japan)
country_stats <- f2f |>
  filter(Country != "Japan") |>
  group_by(iso3, Country) |>
  summarise(
    n_courses = n(),
    n_part    = sum(NbPart, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_women = 100 * sum(NWomen[!is.na(NbPart) & !is.na(NWomen)]) /
                      sum(NbPart[!is.na(NbPart) & !is.na(NWomen)]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

curves_city    <- make_curves(dest)
curves_country <- make_curves(dest_country)
```

## Option A: arrow width = number of courses (one arrow per city)

```{r}
#| label: map-A
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world_p, fill = "grey88", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_path(data = curves_city,
            aes(x, y, group = curve_id, linewidth = n_courses),
            colour = "#c0392b", alpha = 0.7, arrow = arrow_head,
            lineend = "round", linejoin = "round") +
  geom_point(data = dest, aes(px, py), colour = "#c0392b", size = 1.6) +
  geom_text_repel(data = dest, aes(px, py, label = City), size = 3,
                  max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = Inf) +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.3, 2.8), name = "Nb of F2F\ncourses") +
  map_decor +
  labs(title = "Where were F2F courses held? Width = number of courses",
       caption = map_caption)
```

## Option B: arrow colour = number of courses (constant width)

```{r}
#| label: map-B
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world_p, fill = "grey88", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_path(data = make_curves(arrange(dest, n_courses)),   # busiest drawn last
            aes(x, y, group = curve_id, colour = n_courses),
            linewidth = 1, arrow = arrow_head,
            lineend = "round", linejoin = "round") +
  geom_text_repel(data = dest, aes(px, py, label = City), size = 3,
                  max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = Inf) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(option = "C", direction = -1, end = 0.9,
                         name = "Nb of F2F\ncourses") +
  map_decor +
  labs(title = "Where were F2F courses held? Colour = number of courses",
       caption = map_caption)
```

## Option C: countries shaded by number of courses, arrow width = participants

Countries without F2F courses stay grey; Japan (origin) is dark grey.

```{r}
#| label: map-C
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = shade_world(mutate(country_stats, value = n_courses)),
          aes(fill = value), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  japan_layer +
  geom_path(data = curves_city,
            aes(x, y, group = curve_id, linewidth = n_part),
            colour = "grey15", alpha = 0.6, arrow = arrow_head,
            lineend = "round", linejoin = "round") +
  geom_point(data = dest, aes(px, py), colour = "grey15", size = 1.4) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#fcdcd3", high = "#8c1c13", na.value = "grey88",
                      name = "F2F courses\n(country)") +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.3, 3), labels = comma,
                  name = "Arrow width =\nparticipants") +
  map_decor +
  labs(title = "Fill = courses per country, arrow width = participants",
       caption = paste(map_caption, "Japan in dark grey."))
```

## Option H: one map per period (different years)

Countries are shaded by the number of F2F courses held **in that period**; the
arrows (one per city) are sized by the number of courses in the period.
The periods are defined in `period_levels` and can be edited.

```{r}
#| label: map-H
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9.5
period_levels <- c("2015-2018", "2019-2021", "2022-2024", "2025-2026 (partial)")

f2f_p <- f2f |>
  filter(Country != "Japan") |>
  mutate(period = cut(Year, breaks = c(-Inf, 2018, 2021, 2024, Inf),
                      labels = period_levels))

dest_period <- f2f_p |>
  group_by(period, Country, iso3, City, lon, lat) |>
  summarise(n_courses = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  add_xy()

fill_period <- f2f_p |> count(period, iso3, name = "value")

world_period <- do.call(rbind, lapply(period_levels, \(p) {
  world_p |>
    left_join(filter(fill_period, period == p) |> select(iso3, value), by = "iso3") |>
    mutate(period = factor(p, levels = period_levels))
}))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world_period, aes(fill = value), colour = "white",
          linewidth = 0.15) +
  japan_layer +
  geom_path(data = make_curves(dest_period),
            aes(x, y, group = curve_id, linewidth = n_courses),
            colour = "grey10", alpha = 0.6,
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed"),
            lineend = "round", linejoin = "round") +
  geom_point(data = dest_period, aes(px, py), colour = "grey10", size = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~period, ncol = 2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#fcdcd3", high = "#8c1c13", na.value = "grey88",
                      name = "F2F courses\n(country)") +
  scale_linewidth(range = c(0.3, 2.5), name = "Arrow width =\nF2F courses") +
  map_decor +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)) +
  labs(title = "F2F courses outside Japan by period",
       caption = "Japan in dark grey; no arrows for Chiba/Tokyo.")
```
